source: US National Archives and Records Administration, Record Group 242, German Foreign Office records received from St Antony’s College, T136 reel 39.

locator.archival_file: S.A. / Deutschland Nr. 130, Band 7; Die Beziehungen Deutschlands zu Rumaenien
locator.frame_indexing: Four-digit frame number in the official object filename, not a printed folio or PDF page.

finding_aid.visually_checked_entry: Printed column 98: Deutschland 130, volume 7, 1 November 1918–10 August 1919, PS, SA Reel 39.

documents.identity: Telegram copy, General Groener to the Foreign Office through von Hintze; Great Headquarters, 4 November 1918; arrival 5:30 p.m.; signed I.A. Groener; Ia Nr. 11212 Geh.Op.
documents.page_relationship: One document across consecutive frames 410 and 411; the final line of 410 continues at the top of 411.
documents.relevance: Discusses the danger to the Romanian occupation army, movement through Hungary or Galicia, and extending the 14-day evacuation term to four weeks.
documents.limit: Its reference 11212 differs from the eight-part source’s unchanged 11226O6. It is not identified as that report or used to supply its missing text.

documents.identity: Telegram copy, legation councillor to the Foreign Office; Great Headquarters, 4 November 1918, 9:10 p.m.; arrival 9:55 p.m.; Nr. 2733; signed Lersner.
documents.page_relationship: Right-hand page only. The left-hand page closes a different Horstmann document.
documents.relevance: Says Groener reported Mackensen ordered to return to Germany, using Hungarian railways if possible and otherwise marching through Hungary.
documents.limit: Related withdrawal context; no claim that it copies any part of the intercepted eight-part report.

documents.identity: Deciphered telegram, Bukarest via Koenigswusterhausen, 5 November 1918, 9:20 p.m.; arrival 6 November, 12:40 a.m.; Nr. 579; signed Horstmann.
documents.page_relationship: Right-hand page; ends with Horstmann’s signature. The next frame is not assumed to continue it.
documents.relevance: Reports a decision to occupy Kronstadt, Hermannstadt and Transylvanian railways to preserve connections and secure possible withdrawal. This independently corroborates the setting of the accepted fourth-part proposal.
documents.limit: Not a verbatim copy of that fourth part and supplies no source-certified letters for part 6.

limits: Original images and the finding-aid entry were visually inspected. Hashes identify downloaded official JPEG bytes; no new image files are distributed.
The three documents authenticate historical context and archival locations, not the proposed cross-page assembly, its conflicting receipt dates, or an exact shared wording.
No new A6 reading or restoration count is claimed. The primary input and cryptographic certificate remain unchanged.
